guides.wedding-vendor-questions-checklis: Questions to Ask Wedding Vendors Before Signing
The questions that expose hidden fees, cancellation terms and substitution clauses in wedding vendor contracts, organised by vendor type.
Wedding Vendor Questions Checklist
The useful questions are not about style, they are about what happens when something goes wrong. Ask who shows up, what is included, and what triggers an extra charge.
Contract
Named person, backup, arrival time and overtime rate
Money
Tax, service, travel, gratuities and the payment schedule
Risk
Cancellation, postponement, force majeure and refund terms
Deliverables
What you receive, in what format, and by when

Ask the same core set of every vendor so quotes are comparable: is the person you met the person who will attend, what is the backup plan, what is excluded from the price, when is the final count or final detail due, and what happens if you cancel. Get the answers in writing — a verbal assurance is not a contract term.

US contracts commonly separate sales tax, service charge and gratuity, and may include a force majeure clause that limits refunds. UK and EU contracts more often include VAT and must spell out consumer cancellation rights; data protection rules also affect how photographers may use your images. For a destination wedding, ask which country's law governs the contract and whether the deposit is protected by any local scheme.

The clauses that hurt are substitution ('a photographer of equal standard'), vague overtime, and a non-refundable deposit with no rescheduling right. Also ask about vendor meals, parking, power requirements and early access — small logistics that turn into day-of surprises. Never sign before the venue has confirmed that outside vendors are permitted.
What is the most important question to ask?
Who exactly will be present on the day, and what is the backup if they cannot attend. Substitution clauses are the most common source of disappointment.
Should we ask about insurance?
Yes. Many venues require a certificate of insurance from outside vendors, and public liability cover protects you if equipment or a guest is injured.
When should we sign?
After the venue and date are confirmed and you have compared at least two itemised quotes. Never sign a vendor contract that conflicts with the venue's rules.
